definitions.gloss: chief priest of a Shinto shrine
definitions.explanation: The highest-ranking priest who oversees the administration and rituals of a Shinto shrine. Each shrine typically has one chief priest.

examples.japanese: {宮司|ぐうじ}が{祝詞|のりと}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The chief priest read out the Shinto prayer.

examples.japanese: この{神社|じんじゃ}の{宮司|ぐうじ}は{代々|だいだい}{同|おな}じ{家系|かけい}が{務|つと}めている。
examples.english: The chief priest of this shrine has been served by the same family for generations.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}の{祭事|さいじ}に{向|む}けて、{宮司|ぐうじ}が{準備|じゅんび}を{進|すす}めている。
examples.english: The chief priest is making preparations for the New Year festivities.

notes:
USAGE:
{宮司|ぐうじ} is specific to Shinto shrines. The equivalent for a Buddhist temple would be {住職|じゅうしょく} (head priest). Below the {宮司|ぐうじ} in the shrine hierarchy are {禰宜|ねぎ} (senior priest) and {権禰宜|ごんねぎ} (junior priest).

The word combines {宮|ぐう} (shrine/palace) and {司|じ} (to manage/oversee).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宮司|ぐうじ}を{務|つと}める: to serve as chief priest
- {宮司|ぐうじ}{職|しょく}: the position of chief priest
- {神社|じんじゃ}の{宮司|ぐうじ}: chief priest of a shrine
